name: MNN (Alibaba mobile inference engine)
notable_features: A pre-LLM mobile inference engine that grew a real LLM story rather than being replaced by one: the README tracks Qwen2.5-Omni 3B/7B, Qwen3, DeepSeek-R1 1.5B, Qwen3-VL and the Qwen3.5 series (announced 2026-03-05), with shipping MNN Chat apps for Android and iOS and multimodal (text/image/audio) support

THE DIFFERENTIATING BACKEND IS THE HEXAGON DSP. Release 3.6.1 (2026-07-22) added a Qualcomm Hexagon backend for accelerated inference on Hexagon DSPs - a path no GPU-oriented engine in this repo takes, and the reason to know about MNN at all
MNN TaoAvatar (2025-06-11) is a striking demonstration: LLM, ASR, TTS, A2BS and NNR models all running locally on-device with no server component
Designed for the actual constraints of phones: small binary footprint, low memory ceiling, no Python runtime, and shipping as Android/iOS native apps
Battle-tested by Alibaba in consumer products per the project description, which is the real credential
Apache-2.0, 16171 stars, 3.6.1 released 2026-07-23, last push 2026-09-30, 3596 open issues
hardware_caveats: CLOSED MODEL FORMAT. MNN uses its own .mnn representation, converted from ONNX via MNN tools. There is no GGUF, no safetensors, no AWQ/GPTQ path. Converting and validating a quantised model for MNN is your job, and the results will not match your GGUF numbers

The hardware surface is mobile-first. The Hexagon DSP backend is the notable one; Vulkan and OpenCL cover Android GPU; there is a CUDA path but for conversion/validation rather than for phone deployment. No ROCm, no TPU, no npu-in-the-datacentre sense
The LLM models it ships support are small: DeepSeek-R1 1.5B, Qwen2.5-Omni 3B and 7B, Qwen3. This is on-device scale. There is no 70B path and no tensor parallelism

scheduling is 'none' - no continuous batching, no paged KV, no prefix caching. It is a single-stream on-device runtime. The exception is in the models themselves, where MNN implements specific architectures rather than scheduling them
Larger models in the family need mmap and memory pressure management on a phone; memory ceilings on real devices, not on your desktop, are the constraint
3596 open issues on 16171 stars, plus a multi-language codebase (C++, Kotlin, Objective-C++, Swift) that widens the support surface
Quality and model coverage depend on what Alibaba's own product teams have needed - the roadmap visibly follows their phone products, which is fine until your model is not on it
best_for: Shipping an LLM or multimodal model inside an Android or iOS app with no server dependency, which nothing else in this repo does
Mobile CPU, Vulkan or OpenCL inference where the .mnn format and a small footprint are the point
Anyon working with Qualcomm Hexagon DSPs - the 3.6.1 Hexagon backend is a unique capability in this whole slice
An offline fully-local assistant app, as TaoAvatar demonstrates
avoid_for: Server or datacenter inference of any kind - there is no scheduler and the model formats are not the ones you have
Using existing GGUF or safetensors quantisations directly; the conversion step is on you and the numbers will not transfer
Large models; the shipped LLM support tops out at the 7B/8B class
notes: The mobile/embedded half of the niche, and the only project here with a DSP backend. Useful precisely because the LLM-serving field is GPU-CUDA-shaped and phones are not: MNN is what on-device actually looks like, with its own format, its own backends and its own small-model ceiling. The Hexagon DSP backend (3.6.1, 2026-07-22) is the single most unusual hardware capability recorded in this slice.
